doc.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Freddie Hubbard as influence and joining his band
summary: Hubbard was his biggest non-bass influence; after moving to New York in 1989 Carl Allen got him the gig and he stayed two and a half to three years.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Freddie Hubbard. Freddie Hubbard was probably my biggest non-bass influence as far as writing, as far as improvising. I first heard Freddie’s CTI Records like “Red Clay” and all that stuff, and I heard the records he made with Art Blakey and I heard his Blue Note records. And then when I saw him in person I’ll never forget, I almost passed out because I’d never seen anyone play with that much — that was my first time actually witnessing a jazz musician with that much fire playing in person. And I remember I almost fell over in my chair and from that point on I said I want to play with Freddie Hubbard. And it’s amazing how fate happens, because Carl Allen was in the band at that time and Carl Allen and I became best friends and we started working with Benny Green. Actually I started working with Freddie first. I moved to New York in 1989, and Carl knew how bad I wanted to play with Freddie. And their bass player was about to leave the band, so Carl, I was still going to Juilliard at the time, and Carl said, “Hey man, you want to make this gig with Freddie in South Carolina?” I said “What! Yes!” So I joined Freddie’s band and I stayed in his band for about two and a half or three years and that was probably the most memorable musical experience I’ve had in my life.
You got your education right there.
